evidence.quote: Therefore, following periods when inflation has been running below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time.
The change to "shortfalls" clarifies that, going forward, employment can run at or above real-time estimates of its maximum level without causing concern
The persistent undershoot of inflation from our 2 percent longer-run objective is a cause for concern.
By reducing our scope to support the economy by cutting interest rates, the lower bound increases downward risks to employment and inflation.
Of course, when employment is below its maximum level, as is clearly the case now, we will actively seek to minimize that shortfall by using our tools to support economic growth and job creation.
Of course, if excessive inflationary pressures were to build or inflation expectations were to ratchet above levels consistent with our goal, we would not hesitate to act.

parsed.rationale: The new framework commits to overshooting 2 percent after shortfalls and to tolerating strong employment without preemptive tightening. It stresses low-inflation and lower-bound downside risks, a strongly dovish shift only modestly offset by a pledge to act against excessive inflation.
